reason: E1 supports the ductility drop at 400–800°C in single-phase fcc HEAs. E2 supports high HAGB energy and the possibility of decohesion without segregation. However, no cited evidence supports the claims that dynamic grain refinement to 10–50 nm occurs under these conditions, that a shift to grain boundary sliding happens, or that this sliding causes decohesion—these are unsupported mechanistic steps.
premises: Single-phase fcc HEAs exhibit a rapid ductility drop at 400–800°C
High-angle grain boundaries in CoCrFeMnNi have high energy (~0.87 J/m²) and may be prone to decohesion even without segregation
Dynamic grain refinement to ~10–50 nm can occur under high strain rate at intermediate temperatures
Refinement below a critical size shifts deformation from dislocation slip to grain boundary sliding
Grain boundary sliding on high-energy boundaries leads to intergranular decohesion and brittle failure
